claim_text: Islamic historical works preserve a developed narrative about an expedition/engagement at Mu'ta
evidence_summary: Presence of a developed narrative in later Islamic compilations is clear; this is a statement about the tradition, not proof of every event detail.
alternative_explanation: The narrative may combine event memory with later framing

claim_text: Al-Waqidi is the earliest extant detailed Mu'ta account identified by Powers
evidence_summary: Powers identifies Waqidi as the earliest extant detailed account in his comparison.
alternative_explanation: A wider survey of fragments and all surviving source families may refine this

claim_text: Al-Waqidi explicitly states that Mu'ta occurred in Jumada I of year 8 AH
evidence_summary: Powers says Waqidi does not explicitly state month/year in the battle account; placement in the sequence suggests year 8 AH.
alternative_explanation: Another account in the Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham transmission gives a date

claim_text: Ibn Ishaq material transmitted by Ibn Hisham includes a notice placing Mu'ta in Jumada I
alternative_explanation: Powers reports the dated notice and chain ending in Urwa b. al-Zubayr; Arabic edition and transmission variants not yet collated.
confidence: May be a transmitted chronology or later arrangement

claim_text: Theophanes' Chronographia contains a notice of an engagement at Mothous commonly identified with Mu'ta
evidence_summary: The chronicle contains a relevant place-name and event; identification with Mu'ta is still a geographic/textual inference.
alternative_explanation: Mothous may be another place or transmission variant

claim_text: Theophanes' synchronisms date the engagement differently from the conventional Sira chronology
evidence_summary: Modern interpreters read the chronicle's regnal and other synchronisms as associating the report with Abu Bakr's first year; exact conversion must be checked against Greek critical text.
confidence: manuscript or source-chronology problem may explain the divergence

claim_text: Theophanes is an independent non-Islamic witness to the Mu'ta engagement
source_location: Powers pp.82-83; Shoemaker pp.109-110; Conrad 1990 to inspect
evidence_summary: Independence depends on whether his source was a distinct Greek/Syriac tradition or an Arabic/Islamic report transmitted through intermediaries.
alternative_explanation: Could preserve partly independent details even if source transmission crossed traditions
change_reason: Do not assume independence from language alone

claim_text: The traditional Islamic account says the campaign followed the killing of al-Harith b. Umayr al-Azdi
evidence_summary: This is the causal explanation within the Islamic narrative tradition.
alternative_explanation: The reported killing could be one trigger among several; it might also be narrative etiological framing
change_reason: Separate cause in narrative from verified cause

claim_text: No contemporary Syriac account of Mu'ta has yet been identified in the scholarship reviewed
evidence_summary: Shoemaker states that Mu'ta is unattested in Syriac historical tradition or Syriac texts to his knowledge.
alternative_explanation: Limited corpus coverage or lost sources may explain silence; independent corpus review is required
change_reason: Do not turn author's search statement into proof of absence

claim_text: A large regular Byzantine imperial field army fought at Mu'ta
evidence_summary: Sources and modern reconstructions differ; Knauf and Shoemaker question a major regular imperial deployment at the site.
confidence: regional detachments or mixed forces are alternatives

claim_text: The opposing force included local Arab groups associated with the Byzantine frontier
evidence_summary: Knauf reconstructs local tribal participation from the narrative's tribal lists and geography; Shoemaker questions regular Roman troop presence.
alternative_explanation: Imperial units or a mixed local/imperial force remain possible

claim_text: The killing of the envoy was the sole historical cause of the expedition
source_location: Islamic narrative as discussed by Powers
evidence_summary: The source tradition explains the expedition through the envoy's killing; no independent verification or evidence of exclusivity has been found.
reviewed_by: local coalition politics or a wider influence objective could also have mattered
column16: Do not conflate stated cause with complete cause

claim_text: The engagement directly transferred sovereignty over territory to the Islamic polity
evidence_summary: No reviewed evidence demonstrates durable territorial incorporation directly resulting from this engagement.
alternative_explanation: The event may have been punitive
reviewed_by: deterrent or local without territorial acquisition
